title: Observability: add internal metrics for auto-rollback decisioning (lag, monitor errors, rollbacks, false-positive counters)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Background / why
Auto-rollback depends on (a) timely SLO signal, (b) correct monitor resolution, and (c) guardrails that suppress unsafe rollbacks. Today we can’t reliably answer:
- Are we evaluating health on time (or lagging)?
- Are monitor lookups failing/stale and causing “unknown” verdicts?
- How many rollbacks are happening and why?
- How often are we suppressing rollbacks (low traffic/warmup/etc.) and are those suppressions masking real issues?

Goal
Add a small set of first-class internal metrics emitted by rollout-controller so we can:
- detect regressions in evaluator/monitor plumbing,
- quantify rollback volume by cause,
- quantify false-positive risk (suppressed rollbacks + post-hoc “would-have-rolled-back” signals),
- power dashboards + alerting and support post-incident analysis.

Scope
- Add internal metrics in rollout-controller:
  1) Evaluator lag
  2) Monitor fetch errors and staleness
  3) Rollbacks by cause (what triggered)
  4) False-positive / suppression counters
- Ensure metrics are low-cardinality and align with monitor identity contract (route/model/region/tier).
- Wire to existing metrics pipeline and update dashboards where needed.

Non-goals
- Building a new monitoring system or changing SLO definitions.
- High-cardinality per-tenant/per-customer breakdowns by default (allow limited top-level dimensions only).

Proposed metrics (names + types + labels)
All metrics are emitted from rollout-controller.

A) Evaluator lag
- rollout_slo_evaluator_lag_seconds (gauge)
  - Definition: now() - evaluation_window_end_ts for last completed evaluation tick.
  - Labels: env, region
  - Notes: region here is control-plane region (where evaluator runs), not customer workload region.

- rollout_slo_evaluator_tick_duration_seconds (histogram)
  - Definition: wall time per evaluation loop iteration.
  - Labels: env, region

B) Monitor fetch / query health
- rollout_slo_monitor_fetch_requests_total (counter)
  - Labels: env, dependency="monitoring", result="ok|error", error_class="timeout|5xx|4xx|parse|unknown"

- rollout_slo_monitor_fetch_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - Labels: env, dependency="monitoring"

- rollout_slo_monitor_stale_total (counter)
  - Definition: monitor payload fetched but data timestamp older than staleness threshold used by evaluator.
  - Labels: env, reason="stale_timestamp|missing_timestamp|unknown"

- rollout_slo_verdict_unknown_total (counter)
  - Definition: evaluator emits UNKNOWN verdict (vs HEALTHY/UNHEALTHY) because monitor data missing/unavailable.
  - Labels: env, reason="monitor_fetch_error|monitor_stale|monitor_missing|internal_error"

C) Rollback volume + cause
- rollout_auto_rollback_actions_total (counter)
  - Increment on attempted rollback execution (idempotent executor will ensure repeat signals don’t double-count “executed”).
  - Labels:
    - env
    - trigger="latency|error|multiple"
    - cause="threshold_breach|burn_rate_breach|baseline_worse"
    - action_result="executed|no_op_already_rolled_back|blocked_rate_limit|blocked_guardrail|error"

- rollout_auto_rollback_executor_errors_total (counter)
  - Labels: env, error_class="routing_write_failed|conflict|timeout|unknown"

D) False-positive / suppression counters (guardrail observability)
- rollout_auto_rollback_suppressed_total (counter)
  - Increment when evaluator would otherwise roll back but is suppressed.
  - Labels: env, reason="min_traffic_not_met|warmup_window|cooldown_active|baseline_not_worse|monitor_unknown|global_rate_limit"

- rollout_auto_rollback_candidate_breaches_total (counter)
  - Increment when we detect a breach event that would trigger rollback absent suppressions (used to compare against suppressed).
  - Labels: env, trigger="latency|error|multiple"

Label/cardinality guidance
- DO include: env, trigger/cause/reason enums, control-plane region.
- DO NOT include: customer_id, route_id, model_id, deployment_id in default metrics (too high-cardinality).
- If we need deeper cuts, rely on decision trace logs (already in evaluator) and/or sampled structured events, not metrics.

Acceptance criteria
- Metrics are emitted in rollout-controller with documented definitions and stable names.
- No unbounded labels; cardinality checked against staging traffic (confirm no exploding label values).
- Dashboard updates:
  - panel for evaluator lag + tick duration
  - panel for monitor fetch error rate and p95 latency
  - panel for rollbacks by trigger/cause/action_result
  - panel for suppressed rollbacks by reason
- Alerting guidance drafted (not necessarily enabled by default):
  - page/ticket when evaluator lag > 2x evaluation interval for >10m (ticket initially)
  - ticket when monitor fetch errors sustained >1% for >15m

Testing plan
- Unit: metrics emitted on each code path (HEALTHY/UNHEALTHY/UNKNOWN, suppressions, executor outcomes).
- Integration (staging):
  - simulate monitor outage -> verdict_unknown_total increments; monitor_fetch_requests_total{result=error} increments.
  - simulate stale monitor data -> monitor_stale_total increments.
  - simulate breach + suppression (min traffic) -> candidate_breaches_total increments and suppressed_total{reason=min_traffic_not_met} increments.

Rollout plan
- Ship behind existing auto-rollback feature flag (metrics always-on in staging, production gated by controller config).
- Verify dashboards in internal environment for 48h before enabling in prod clusters.

Links
- Related PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-18511.json ("Add internal metrics (evaluator lag, monitor fetch errors, rollbacks by cause) and update dashboards wiring")
- Dependent work:
  - ENG-2314 (evaluator algorithm + verdict reasons)
  - ENG-2315 (executor idempotency/rate limits; action_result values)

Open questions
- Do we want a separate metric for “rollback recommended but blocked by global safety limits” vs general suppression? (Currently modeled via suppressed_total{reason=global_rate_limit} and rollback_actions_total{action_result=blocked_rate_limit}.)
- Do we need per-workload-region dimensions? (Avoiding for now; can add sampled events instead if needed.)
comments: 2025-02-07 (Caleb Johnson): Drafted metric set + label guidance. Key concern is route/model labels blowing up cardinality; proposing enums-only + rely on decision trace logs for deep dives.
2025-02-10 (Allison Grant): +1 on enums-only. Please ensure we split monitor fetch failures (network/5xx) vs staleness vs missing monitor so SRE can distinguish outages from config gaps.

2025-02-12 (Miles Thornton): For game day we need a quick way to see whether suppressions are doing work. Suggested adding candidate_breaches_total so we can compute suppression rate = suppressed/candidate.

2025-02-14 (Caleb Johnson): Implemented metrics in rollout-controller and added dashboard wiring. Sent PR for review. Also aligned verdict_unknown_total reasons with evaluator’s "UNKNOWN" reason codes.
2025-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): Please default alerts to ticketing until we have baseline after GA. Paging on evaluator lag should be P2 after we validate it doesn’t flap during deploys.
2025-02-21 (Caleb Johnson): Landed PR-18511. Verified staging dashboards: evaluator lag stable (<5s), monitor fetch error rate ~0.02%. Marking Done.
